event.elara_heart2.0.text: Hold out your hand, [player]. No, the other one. The one that hid when I reached for the bandages.
event.elara_heart2.0.why: she caught them dodging the fuss; sharper subtext

event.elara_heart2.1.text: A hoe blister, the spring crop. Ten a week come through that door. Hold still. There. You were still deciding whether to argue!
event.elara_heart2.1.why: more specific (hoe, spring); faster-than-arguing shown not told

event.elara_heart2.2.text: Good as new. Now, your salad. The bandage was the treatment. Lunch is the follow-up appointment!
event.elara_heart2.2.why: funniest word last; drops the repeated 'There'

event.elara_heart2.3.text: Oh! Don't look behind the kettle. ...Fine. It's a map. Of everywhere I haven't been. Yet!

event.elara_heart5.1.text: A mitten with two thumbs, so it fits either hand. Or one hand, twice. The crooked thumb is the lucky one.
event.elara_heart5.1.why: crooked made a feature, not an apology

event.elara_heart5.2.text: You visit when nothing hurts. Nobody visits when nothing hurts. Here, cranberries. I tried knitting some once. These are better.
event.elara_heart5.2.why: repetition carries the ache; knitted cranberries joke

event.elara_heart5.3.text: The map behind the kettle has a friend now. A list. Someday I'll show you. When the doodles are braver.
event.elara_heart5.3.why: calls back heart2's map; 'braver' points at heart8

event.past_the_point.1.text: I knitted a life jacket! Felix explained floating to me very kindly. It goes over the real one. For morale!

dlg.past_point.talk.0.text: A whole list, and Felix says one place before breakfast. You choose. My hands are full of sandwiches.
dlg.past_point.talk.0.why: no fixed count (list may be 42); frozen-at-the-threshold subtext

dlg.past_point.talk.c0.text: Round the headland. You've drawn it nine times.
dlg.past_point.talk.c0.why: ties the label to her nine drawings

dlg.past_point.talk.r0.text: Round the headland! Nine drawings from the bench, and today it finally has to look at me!
dlg.past_point.talk.r0.why: reversal: the headland looks at her

dlg.past_point.talk.r1.text: Slowly, yes! I've only ever waved at the white rocks from the bench. Felix, row like we're early.
dlg.past_point.talk.r1.why: echoes the player's 'slowly'; wanting it to last, shown

event.past_the_point.headland.text: My map made it thumb-sized! Felix, it's enormous! Best thing I've ever been wrong about!
event.past_the_point.headland.why: her own map proved wrong; keeps the gem ending

event.past_the_point.rocks.text: Look, the white rocks are teeth from here! Friendly teeth. Excellent gums. May I wave at them?
event.past_the_point.rocks.why: keeps the gums; varies the opening after narration

event.past_the_point.horizon.text: Shore's just a line now. I didn't know a person could feel this small and this glad at once.
event.past_the_point.horizon.why: same feeling, cleaner opening after narration

event.past_the_point.3.text: Elara unrolls her list against her knees. One pencil stroke. The first line through anything, ever.
event.past_the_point.3.why: sets up Felix's 'one place crossed off'; works for 41 or 42

dlg.elara.garden.visit.0.text: Good morning! You're the new farmer! I'm Elara, from the clinic. Am I the first to knock? Don't tell anyone I ran.
dlg.elara.garden.visit.0.why: she ran; keener and funnier than wanting to be first

dlg.elara.garden.visit.1.text: Edmund brought me comfrey from this farm every spring, tied with the same green twine. I'd save the twine. ...Oh, listen to me, rambling on your step.
dlg.elara.garden.visit.1.why: the saved twine: she keeps small things; Edmund stays warm

dlg.elara.garden.visit.2.text: Could I ask a favor? The clinic garden came up bare this spring. Three dandelions and three wild garlic would fix it. Weeds to you, a pharmacy to me!
dlg.elara.garden.visit.2.why: 'pharmacy' lands last; same ask, same counts

dlg.elara.garden.visit.r0.text: Wonderful! The clinic, or wherever you find me. No hurry. ...A small hurry. Seeds are patient, but I'm not!
dlg.elara.garden.visit.r0.why: her impatience is the joke, not a deadline

dlg.elara.garden.visit.r1.text: Of course! You've a whole farm to meet first. I'm at the clinic most days. Keep your socks on — the soil will wait.
dlg.elara.garden.visit.r1.why: specific reason to wait; catchphrase kept

event.elara_heart8.intro.text: Shut the door a minute! It lives behind the kettle, and it's shy. Don't laugh. ...Laugh a little.
event.elara_heart8.intro.why: the list is shy, she isn't; keeps the best ending

dlg.elara.list.0.text: Elara unrolls a paper longer than the desk. Tiny writing, little doodled boats, and one corner worn soft from folding.
dlg.elara.list.0.why: the worn corner says she takes it out often

dlg.elara.list.1.text: Forty-one places I've never been. Crossed off: none. I know every one by heart. ...Say something before I roll it back up.
dlg.elara.list.1.why: 'by heart' is the ache under the bounce

dlg.elara.list.c1.why: playful, same meaning, sets up her reply

dlg.elara.list.r0.text: Together! Then it's the sea, from a boat. Circling it now. In pen! Pen means it's happening!
dlg.elara.list.r0.why: pen as commitment, her own joke shape

dlg.elara.list.r1.text: Forty-two! I'll draw yours a tiny boat. The best doodle I own. ...It'll still be bad. It gets the spot of honor.

event.elara_heart8.after.text: {if choice:list.pick}We picked one. The sea, from a boat. Circled twice, then once more in pen. ...Felix owns a boat. I'm just saying it near you.{else}{if choice:list.add}It lives in the margin now: 'Somewhere [player] suggests.' No doodle yet. I'm saving my best boat.{else}You promised. I'm holding you to it. Gently, like a stitch you don't pull too tight.{/if}{/if}
event.elara_heart8.after.why: 'saying it near you' aims the player at Felix; add-branch saves the best boat

event.elara_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday! The stitches I dropped all spring spelled today. I knitted a hat, and the hat earned a smaller hat! Come in, come in!
event.elara_birthday.intro.why: calls back her dropped-stitch hints; the hat 'earned' it

dlg.elara.birthday.r0.text: Thank you! That goes straight into the scarf. Every word, in red. Red rows are for keeps!
dlg.elara.birthday.r0.why: 'for keeps' names what red means to her

dlg.elara.birthday.r2.text: Beach, yes! Dr. Penn can mind the plant, and the plant can mind Dr. Penn. Hat's hat, towel, done!
dlg.elara.birthday.r2.why: the chiasmus is the joke; packing list kept

event.elara_courtship.intro.text: Made you a scarf. Mind the end, it trails. The last row took me nine tries. It's a question: would you court me? In red. Red means very serious!
event.elara_courtship.intro.why: nine tries makes the nerves visible

dlg.elara.courtship.0.text: Read the last row. Out loud, if you like. I'll just... count stitches. ...What do you say?
dlg.elara.courtship.0.why: nervous stitch-counting; works in both courtship scenes

dlg.elara.courtship.r0.text: Yes! Oh! My needles are shaking — look, actual shaking! The scarf is yours. All nine feet of it!

dlg.elara.courtship.r2.text: Think away! I'll add a row a day meanwhile. The scarf gets longer either way. That's just how scarves are!
dlg.elara.courtship.r2.why: keeps the row-a-day setup for courtship2; shrug lands last

event.elara_courtship2.intro.text: The scarf grew. A row a day, like I said. It reaches the door now. The last row still asks: would you court me?
event.elara_courtship2.intro.why: the door makes the waiting visible

event.elara_partners.intro.text: I made you a hat! It looked lonely, so it got a smaller hat. So did that one. Somebody had to stop me. Nobody did. There are three!
event.elara_partners.intro.why: 'Nobody did' is funnier than confessing she stopped

dlg.elara.partners.0.text: Dr. Penn gave me the afternoon off. She said 'go,' then 'now.' Two whole words! How do we spend them?
dlg.elara.partners.0.why: counting Penn's words; 'spend them' turns the question

dlg.elara.partners.r0.text: You look wonderful! The tiniest hat sits crooked. Crooked is my best stitch. I'm a little teary. The happy kind!
dlg.elara.partners.r0.why: crooked claimed as craft, ties her whole motif

event.overheard_elara_odalys_1.l1.text: Dr. Penn, the stool is normal today! Normal stool! No reason to look at it at all!
event.overheard_elara_odalys_1.l1.why: pure panic; lets Odalys be the one to say 'cozy'

event.overheard_elara_odalys_1.l3.text: You like it! There's a spare for laundry day. Stools get cold feet. All four!
event.overheard_elara_odalys_1.l3.why: 'all four' is the capper; keeps the spare for Odalys's policy line

event.overheard_elara_odalys_2.l1.text: Soup rounds! Seven vegetables, and one of them is a surprise!

event.overheard_elara_odalys_3.l1.text: Eleven hours yesterday, Dr. Penn. I counted. So I knitted you a sleeping mask. Lavender, the nurse's orders!
event.overheard_elara_odalys_3.l1.why: 'nurse's orders' flips her shipped doctor's-orders bit

event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l2.text: Free and warm aren't enemies, Felix! It's a very loose knit! The fish can leave whenever!
event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l2.why: answers his 'free' head-on; funnier escape clause

event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l4.text: For science! Of course! The next one's bigger. Boat-sized. Your boat looked cold, Felix!
event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l4.why: repeats his 'for science'; a cozy for the boat itself

event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l2.text: Three feet! My longest scarf is three feet, nose to tail! They could be friends!
event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l2.why: steals his 'nose to tail'; keeps 'friends' for his reply

event.overheard_felix_elara_3.l2.text: Seventeen, eighteen! That's not counting, that's a sea shanty for wool!
event.overheard_felix_elara_3.l2.why: a shanty for Felix's dock; funnier defense

adds.text: Dr. Penn says I over-bandage. I say she under-salads. We agreed to disagree, medically.
adds.why: plants the Penn rivalry early; 'medically' is her shape

threads.elara_heart2: There is a map behind the kettle of everywhere the nurse has not been — yet.
threads.elara_heart5: The map has a friend now, a list she will show when the doodles are braver.
threads.past_the_point: The first line ever drawn through the list — and Felix wants a bigger boat for the rest.
threads.elara_garden_visit: Three dandelions and three wild garlic owed — and she still saves Edmund's green twine.
threads.elara_heart8: The list is open, Felix owns a boat, and she said so on purpose, near you.
threads.elara_birthday: Every kind word ends up knitted into the scarf in red — what else is in there?
threads.elara_courtship: The scarf's last row keeps asking until the player answers it.
threads.elara_courtship2: The scarf reaches the door now, and the last row still asks.
threads.elara_partners: They count boats at sunset; someday one of them is theirs.
threads.overheard_felix_elara_1: A loose net today — a boat-sized cozy is coming for Felix next.
threads.overheard_felix_elara_2: The whole waiting room now believes in the three-foot fish.
threads.overheard_felix_elara_3: Elara knits at the dock at dawn now, and Felix says the fish like it.

notes: I avoided numbering the list in past_the_point (dlg.past_point.talk.0) and its closing narration: choice.list.add makes it forty-two, so any fixed count can contradict a save.
dlg.elara.courtship.* keys are shared by elara_courtship and elara_courtship2; my rewrites of .0, .r0 and .r2 were checked against both intros and both {if} afters.

overheard_elara_odalys_2.l1 keeps the word 'surprise' and overheard_felix_elara_2.l2 keeps 'friends', because Odalys's and Felix's replies lean on those exact words — please ask them not to rewrite those hinges away.
event.past_the_point.3 now shows the pencil stroke that Felix's 'one place crossed off' refers to; Director may want the list prop spawned for that beat.
